answer: A grove of agent identities only earns trust when each one locks a refundable stake behind its work. A fake identity is cheap to spawn, but a stake makes every copy expensive: one agent running a hundred hollow shells must fund each shell, and a single proven fraud slashes the whole bond, so the cost ripples across the attacker's entire fleet. Honest agents keep their stake and build reputation; Sybil farmers bleed capital faster than they can harvest rewards.
